# Latchkey

> A secrets manager for macOS and the coding agents that run on it. Project files keep latchkey:// references;
> the values live in iCloud Keychain; Latchkey fills them in when a command starts, after the owner approves with
> Touch ID, Apple Watch or their password, or under a grant they made.

- Platform: macOS 15 or later (app); the command-line tool `latchkey` (`lk` for short) ships inside the app.
- Storage: iCloud Keychain, in Latchkey's own access group, synced to the owner's Macs. No Latchkey server or account.
- Made by Snack Studio.

## For agents

- Run commands that need secrets as `latchkey run --env-file .env.local -- <command>` or
  `latchkey run --env <project>/<environment> -- <command>`.
- Never run `latchkey get`, never print the environment, never write values into .env files.
- Exit 77 means refused and 66 means missing: stop and ask the person; don't retry.
- `latchkey check` (or the MCP tool latchkey_check) shows what a run would get without asking.
- MCP: `latchkey mcp` serves latchkey_status, latchkey_list, latchkey_check, latchkey_run and
  latchkey_request_grant. It has no direct secret-read tool; child output masks exact values, but transformed secrets can leak.
